        Source-dual endpoint-generator existence, with the same zero-radical case split.

        Exact classification of forbidden crosses for one arrow #

        For a length-one landing in the opposite closed zigzag, a forbidden cross cannot have both outer paths equal to identities: the landing itself would then be a path through the supposedly empty middle Hom. Since all paths have length at most one, every cross therefore has an outgoing arrow on its left or an incoming arrow on its right. The following two submodules make that source-level dichotomy explicit.

        Submodule k (D.obj X' ⟶ D.obj Y')

            forbiddenCrossSubmodule D X' Y' ≤ outgoingArrowCrossSubmodule D X' Y' ⊔ incomingArrowCrossSubmodule D X' Y'

            The forbidden cross space for a length-one landing is generated by the two BGRS p.240 cross types: a competing outgoing arrow followed by an ambient map, or an ambient map followed by a competing incoming arrow.

            This theorem records only the exact path-shape classification. Removing the cases where an outer arrow is the landing itself uses endpoint-radical factorization; identifying the remaining arrow with the adjacent closed-chain ray uses the concrete chain indexing.
